unmatched.line: Module 9/10 Lab
Module 9/10 Lab

Through group discussion and collaboration, prepare a ten-slide (maximum) presentation addressing your Assignment Topic. The presentation should build on the readings, lecture material, the mid-term essay and insights provided by guest speakers. The deck must summarize the issues at play and their background, identify key perspectives on the issue and propose a solution to it. The presentation must also include an analysis of the proposed solution’s federal-provincial implications, its implications for key stakeholder groups, its gender implications, and a general indication of how the proposed approach would be implemented. The deck should describe two not-recommended options but does not need to discuss them in depth. The deck is to be submitted as a group assignment. In the event that the group is not able to agree on a recommended option (it happens sometimes but is to be avoided if possible) the deck should present however many “recommended options” there are. Group members will all receive identical marks. Each deck will be presented in class on March 25 th in a “mock Cabinet” format.

There are 17 assigned readings during Weeks 1 to 10. For each reading, there will be in-class time to hand-write and submit a short reading response, and there will be in-class time for discussion. You will receive one grade for these activities on Friday March 20 (Week 10), based on the quantity and quality of your in-class reading responses and in-class participation. You will also receive an interim grade and feedback on Friday February 13. The interim grade has no weight.

If you wish to request an alternative to Turnitin, you must email me ( Christopher.Lowry@uwaterloo.ca ) by Friday January 23 (the end of Week 3). Instead of submitting your term paper on Learn, you will email it directly to me on the due date. Further, if your term paper is selected for the April 2 in-class workshop, then your responding to questions will be worth 10% (instead of 20%) and you will also have an individual oral exam worth 10%. If your term paper is not selected, then your individual oral exam will be doubled in length to allow for more questions (no change to the weighting).
